title: Stability of the bribery set
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $f$ be a Boolean function on sign vectors of length $n$, and let $q$ be a real target. For a nonnegative integer $t$, let $J_t$ be the set obtained by starting with the empty set and, at each step, adding a coordinate of maximum influence if the uniform mean of $f$ after replacing the coordinates in the current set by $1$ is below $q$, and otherwise keeping the set unchanged. If that mean at step $t$ is at least $q$, then $J_{t+s}=J_t$ for every nonnegative integer $s$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on sign vectors of length $n$
The uniform mean after bribing the set at step $t$ is at least $q$
